full_judgment:
6. Defendant Nos.1-4 contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and contending inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury. He appointed Puma Chandra Adhikary as the 'Purohit' in his house. As the consideration for his religious service Raja Mahendra Ranjan gave him nishkar pattan of 1.19 acres of land of CS Khatian No.176 for permanently residing therein as well as for maintenance of his livelihood. Accordingly, the said land described in Schedule 'Kha' was recorded in his name in CS Khatian No.176. He possessed 22 decimals of the land of Plot No.69 by making a homestead thereon, by performing religious rites towards the Deity established in the land of Plot No.70 and by cultivating 91 decimals of the land of Plot No.67. RS Khatian No.188 was duly published in his name. At the request of the people in general belonging to the Hindu Religion, Puma Chandra dedicated, by registered Deed of Gift No.6704 dated 6-11-1996, 32 decimals of land from Plot No.67 and 52 decimals from Plot No.91 to the Radha-Gobinda Deity. He died leaving behind his three sons namely, Prabhat, Ashutosh and Shachin. Shachin and Ashutosh gifted their share to defendant No.4 by registered Deed of Gift No.1657 dated 25-2-1998. The defendants have title and possession over the 'Ka' schedule land. The defendants have been possessing the shops established in the suit land and also filed Other Suit No.110 of 2002 for a decree of permanent injunction as the plaintiff threatened to forcibly dispossess them from the suit property. The plaintiff has no title and possession in the suit land and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 18. But it is the case of the defendant-opposite parties that Puma Chandra Adhikary, their predecessor was the 'Purohit' of Zamindar Raja Mahendra and as the consideration of his religious service, the Zamindar gave him 'niskar pattan' of 1.90 acres of land of CS Khatian No.176 for permanently residing therein and maintenance of his livelihood. It is their further case that at the request of the local people, in general, belonging to the Hindu Religion, he dedicated by registered Deed of Gift No.6704 dated 6-11-1996 in total 84 decimals of land to the Radha-Gobinda Jew Bigraha. Thus, from the case of the defendant-opposite parties, it appears that the suit property was beyond the debutter property. But it has already been found that the entire property of CS Khatian No.175 and its Sub-Khatian No.176 is debutter property. At this stage, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that as per the CS Khatians, the property was under the control and management of Courts of Wards and not under the control and management of the Sebait and the predecessor of the opposite parties was a Chakran Purohit under the Courts of Wards. However, they could not produce any evidence to prove that they were ever tenant under the Court of Wards. Moreover, as per sections 6 and 7 of the Courts of Wards Act, 1879, no Debutter property can be claimed by any Court of Wards. However, the Court of Wards also claimed on behalf of the Deity.
